title: Data Classes, Enums, and Sealed Models

scout.purpose: Kotlin provides specialised types for value records, fixed labels, and closed alternatives; choosing the right one makes invalid states harder to express.
scout.realWorldUse: Compose UI state, repository results, navigation destinations, and user actions frequently use immutable data classes and sealed hierarchies.
scout.outcome: Choose data, enum, and sealed types based on identity and alternatives, then handle closed states exhaustively.

blocks.text: A data class is suited to records whose meaning comes primarily from their property values. The compiler provides value-based equals, hashCode, toString, component functions, and copy. Prefer val properties so a state transition creates a new value instead of mutating shared state. copy is shallow: nested mutable objects are still shared unless they are also replaced or designed immutably. Data classes do not validate automatically; constructor and factory rules still matter.

blocks.code:
data class ExpenseDraft(
    val category: String = "",
    val amountText: String = "",
    val note: String = "",
)

val initial = ExpenseDraft()
val edited = initial.copy(category = "Travel")
blocks.caption: copy expresses one immutable state change while preserving the untouched properties.

blocks.title: Value or identity?
rows: Are two instances equal when their fields match?
Does one long-lived object own changing behaviour?
Is there exactly one named instance?
Is this a fixed named option?

blocks.text: Use an enum when each alternative is a singleton of the same simple concept, such as an expense category or sort direction. Enum entries may have properties and functions, but large amounts of entry-specific behaviour can become difficult to scan. Persisting enum ordinal values is fragile because reordering entries changes their numbers. Prefer a stable explicit code when an enum crosses storage or network boundaries, and define how unknown future values are handled.

blocks.code:
enum class ExpenseCategory(val storageCode: String) {
    FOOD("food"),
    TRAVEL("travel"),
    EQUIPMENT("equipment"),
}

fun ExpenseCategory.displayName(): String =
    name.lowercase().replaceFirstChar(Char::uppercase)
blocks.caption: A stable storage code is separate from declaration order and presentation text.

blocks.title: Boundary stability
blocks.text: Names, ordinals, and display labels can change. Persist an intentional stable representation and parse unknown input safely.

sections.title: Sealed types model closed alternatives with different data

blocks.text: A sealed class or interface limits direct alternatives to a known set, letting when check exhaustiveness. Unlike enum entries, each alternative can carry different data. A load result may be Loading, Success with expenses, or Failure with an explanation. The closed hierarchy documents every state the consumer must consider. Do not use a sealed type for an ecosystem intended to accept third-party implementations; the restriction is valuable only when the set should be controlled.

blocks.caption: Every result carries appropriate data and when covers the complete closed set without else.

steps.label: Value record?
steps.detail: Use a data class when properties define equality.

steps.label: Fixed constants?
steps.detail: Use an enum for simple singleton options.

steps.label: Different payloads?
steps.detail: Use a sealed hierarchy for closed alternatives.

steps.label: Open extension?
steps.detail: Use an interface when external implementations are valid.

trap_check.mistake: Using a data class with publicly mutable nested collections.
trap_check.why: copy can share the same mutable collection, so changes leak between supposedly independent values.
trap_check.fix: Expose read-only immutable data or replace nested values during a transition.

trap_check.mistake: Persisting an enum ordinal as permanent data.
trap_check.why: Reordering or inserting entries changes ordinals and corrupts meaning.
trap_check.fix: Persist a stable explicit code and parse it deliberately.

challenge_intro.task: Create an immutable draft, a category enum with stable codes, and a sealed validation result that lists every failure or carries a valid Expense.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Draft updates use copy rather than public mutation. Category persistence does not depend on enum ordinal. Validation result handling is exhaustive without a catch-all else.

recall.prompt: What does data-class copy not guarantee?
recall.answer: It does not deep-copy nested mutable objects.

recall.prompt: When is an enum preferable to a sealed type?
recall.answer: When alternatives are simple fixed singleton constants with the same shape.

recall.prompt: Why can when omit else for a sealed hierarchy?
recall.answer: The compiler knows the controlled set of direct alternatives and can verify coverage.

objectives: Use data classes for immutable value-oriented records.
Represent stable simple options with explicit enum codes.
Model closed outcomes with exhaustive sealed hierarchies.
